summary: The seam between the Phase 7/8 builder (Library + Create Site) and the Phase 9 builder (full-site content generation) is closed and the journey is proven end to end in a real browser against the real operator app. Three gaps were found and fixed, not narrated: (1) Create Site's only wired provider was FakeContentGenerator, so ONE BRIEF produced a site whose every text slot read "Fake …" — a new brief-driven writer (src/content-injection/brief-writer.ts) now composes the draft from the operator's own brief and is the DEFAULT; (2) the Visual Editor seeded its preview from authored.slotValues ALONE, so a freshly created site opened showing the SOURCE site's copy while the production bake would have shipped the draft — the editor now layers the content run's overlay under the authored edits, in the same order src/production/bake.ts stacks them, and the inspector reports which layer a value came from; (3) Create Site defaulted its siteId to the HOST SLUG, so a second Create Site from the same template re-prepared the first customer's project — measured on the first journey run, which wrote data/linear.app/release-projects/linear.app; the site id now comes from the brief's working name and the API reports `reprepared` so "created" is never an unverifiable claim. CORRECTION PASS (Phase 9/10 verifier returned FAIL on three recorded findings; all three are fixed IN CODE and the numbers here are re-measured, not carried over): (4) the writer was blind to slot semantics and filled the pricing table, the changelog date column and the compliance labels with adjectives — value-shaped slots are now either kept verbatim (chrome) or named as needs-input quoting the source figure (fact-bearing), 0 overwritten of 443; (5) a SOURCE statistic ('50%') shipped on an editable customer-facing slot with no decision recorded — the truth mode now records `source-fact-carried-over` in both modes and refuses it under verified-only, and the writer withholds it a layer earlier; (6) the phase's headline denominator was not guarded by its own suite — slot-accounting.json now derives the expected population from the template itself, `templateCoverage.complete` is part of `reconciled`, and the verifier's exact mutation now fails seven checks. The draft after the fixes: 3,079 in-scope slots reconcile, 1,491 filled, 924 changed, UNRESOLVED = 20 (4 external destinations + 16 fact-bearing value-shaped slots), requirements 271 -> 287. It fills fewer slots and blocks on more, deliberately.

briefUsed.goal: We are launching the marketing site for Millwright, a B2B AI workflow company for discrete manufacturing. We sell to plant operations, quality and maintenance leaders at mid-size manufacturers who are running production on whiteboards, paper travellers and three disconnected systems. The site has to explain, without hype, that Millwright puts machine data, work orders, standard work and quality checks on one running plan that updates while the line is still moving — and it has to end every page by asking the reader to book a plant walkthrough with our team.

limitations: THE WRITER IS NOT A MODEL. It is a deterministic compositional writer; there is no LLM key in this repo. It REPEATS: 917 text values written from 342 distinct strings (37%) on the corrected run of the same brief and template — measured by BriefContentGenerator.writerStats(), not estimated. CORRECTED CLAIM: the earlier description 'coherent, on-brand, length-matched' did not survive the verifier, who found the pricing table, the changelog date column and the compliance labels filled with adjectives. That class is now withheld rather than written (see valueShapedSlots); what remains is ordinary prose repetition, which is a quality ceiling, not a wrong-kind-of-value defect.

THE VALUE-SHAPE CLASSIFIER IS A PATTERN SET, NOT AN UNDERSTANDING. It recognises prices, percentages, multipliers, counted quantities, certifications, bylines, dates, times, versions, bare numerics and glyphs in source values up to 60 characters. A value-shaped slot it does not recognise would still be written over, and a sentence containing a figure is deliberately still rewritten. Measured on this template: 443 of 2,441 text slots classify as value-shaped, 0 were overwritten, 16 became named needs-input. Nothing claims the class is complete.

A WITHHELD FACT-BEARING SLOT STILL RENDERS THE SOURCE DEFAULT until the operator decides it — that is what `unresolved` means everywhere in this engine, and it is why the release state is INPUTS_REQUIRED with 287 requirements. The draft does not silently ship the source's price as the customer's; it blocks on it.

Some composed headlines still read awkwardly ('Standard work, standardized.'). The phrase bank is a heuristic with no part-of-speech tagger behind it; three rules (clause-bounded pairs, preserved adjacency, a blocklist) cut the worst of it after a browser run showed 'Leaders mid-size' and 'Telling same' on a real page, but it is a heuristic and it will produce more.

NO BROWSER LAYOUT QA over the created site. runContentLayoutQa was not run on the Millwright draft; values are written to roughly the character length of the string they replace, which is the only offline mitigation. Carried forward from Phase 9's identical gap.

1,493 of the 3,079 slots stay human-required, and 130 text slots still contain the source brand token — every one of them review-flagged. The draft does not resolve review slots and this phase did not opt them in.

The journey template (linear.app) has NO structure-only routes, so int.structureOnlyRespected is proven on the stripe route-policy template through the content stage only; its interaction with a live production compile is still unexercised, exactly as the Phase 8 handoff already named.
/api/create-site now parses the brief with ContentBriefSchema, but the suite has NO negative test for a malformed brief; the rejection path is typechecked and reasoned, not measured.

The suite leaves data/linear.app/release-projects/millwright plus its content run, production spec and production build on disk, and removes only the project directory at the start of the next run. Production specs/builds accumulate per run — the same behaviour every other release-touching suite here has.

OBSERVED, NOT FIXED: a straight `cp` of a release project keeps its recorded projectId, so the copy and the original report the same `siteKey` — which SiteEntrySchema documents as the one key guaranteed unique. data/linear.app/release-projects/wr28-verifier-authored already collides with wr28-assets-stage on disk today. This suite avoids creating another instance by opening an existing project instead of copying one; the underlying scan behaviour is untouched and reported here.

FIXED DURING THIS PHASE, NAMED SO IT IS NOT MISTAKEN FOR A CLEAN FIRST RUN: the first journey run wrote data/linear.app/release-projects/linear.app because Create Site inherited release:prepare's host-slug default site id. That directory was created by this build and has been deleted, and the registry rebuilt (27 site entries, back to the pre-run set plus millwright).

valueShapedSlots.fix: src/content-injection/brief-writer.ts classifies a source value's SHAPE before composing anything. FACT-BEARING shapes (price, percentage, multiplier, counted-quantity, certification, attribution) are never overwritten and never silently kept — they become NAMED needs-input quoting the source figure, unless the brief supplies a `figure` fact for the slot. CHROME shapes (date, time, relative-time, version, numeric-chrome, glyph) are kept verbatim as derived-copy. A sentence that merely contains a figure is still copy and is still rewritten.
